feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: Ousted Paraguayan president appears before prosecutors
entry.summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was removed from office and placed under house arrest Friday. The Senate voted on his impeachment after the collapse of a state-affiliated bank.

entry.title: How the new Senate majority shifts control over the federal judiciary
entry.summary: The change in the Senate's majority party means that starting Jan. 3, Democrats will run federal judicial appointments and may continue to until at least 2030.

entry.title: GOP's lame-duck clock is ticking
entry.summary: The current Congress, under its Republican majorities, must address the National Defense Authorization Act and a government funding bill as Democrats wait to take over.

entry.title: Border shift: Hispanic voters drive Texas' historic flip to blue
entry.summary: Once reliably a red state, Texas will turn deep blue following this week's midterms. One of the most notable shifts was along the Texas-Mexico border, where Hispanic voters had a big influence.

entry.title: Week in Politics: Trump taps Miller for chief of staff; doubles down on Trumpism
entry.summary: President Trump's decision to make Stephen Miller his new chief of staff is a rebuke of the midterm results and a doubling-down on Trumpism.

entry.title: Deb Haaland's New Mexico challenge
entry.summary: Deb Haaland is the first Native American governor of New Mexico. She faces big expectations and challenges, but also opportunities in a deep blue state with abundant petroleum revenue.

entry.title: Defiance Mayor Mike McCann on how Republicans can regroup after midterm losses
entry.summary: Republicans were routed in the midterm elections. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Mike McCann, the Mayor of Defiance, Ohio, about how the Republican party can win back support.

entry.title: An unexpected activist emerged to help block a $5 billion data center in Maryland
entry.summary: Thousands across the U.S. have gotten involved to oppose data centers. One is a Maryland woman who'd been evicted after a pay cut and became a leader of a community effort that blocked a vast project.

entry.title: American democracy was a big winner in the midterms
entry.summary: Results are still outstanding House and Senate races but political scientists say one of the big winners in the mid-terms is American democracy itself.

entry.title: What to know about Gina Hinojosa, Texas' first Latina governor-elect
entry.summary: Gina Hinojosa, state representative from the Rio Grande Valley whose legislative priority has been boosting the public education system, will become the first Latina governor of Texas.
